title: Definitions and Cases: Increase Measured for a Retention Concession when Parking Rent Increases Come Close Together
content:
**Definition.** For a retention concession on a Vehicle, RV & Boat Parking Agreement, the increase the shares are applied to is measured against how recently the rent last changed before the most recent increase:

(a) where the agreement's rent last changed less than 18 months before the notice date of the most recent increase, it is the combined increase of every rent increase noticed on the agreement in the last 24 months — the total of their new rents less the total of their previous rents;

(b) where the rent last changed at least 18 months but less than 24 whole calendar months before that notice date, it is the noticed increase plus half (50%) of the other increases noticed in the last 24 months;

(c) in every other case, no adjustment under this definition.

The noticed increase is the new rent of the most recent rent increase notice less the rent before it. Months are whole calendar months, counted to the same day of the later month; the rent's last change is read from the agreement's last rent change date. A window of the last 24 months covers increase notices dated less than 24 whole calendar months before the handling date.

### Cases (hypothetical)

Increase noticed 3 weeks ago: $190.00 to $205.00 (noticed increase $15.00). An earlier increase, noticed inside the 24-month window: $180.00 to $190.00 ($10.00). The three rows vary only the agreement's last rent change date.

| Rent last changed, before the recent notice date | Increase measured |
|---|---|
| 14 months | (a) $10.00 and $15.00 combined: $25.00 |
| 19 months | (b) $15.00 plus half of $10.00: $20.00 |
| 26 months | (c) no adjustment |

Where the earlier increase had been noticed 25 whole months before the handling date it would lie outside the 24-month window and would not enter (a) or (b).
